newsitem.title: USA: Coke Enterprises up on smaller loss.
newsitem.headline: Coke Enterprises up on smaller loss.

text.p: Shares in Coca-Cola Enterprises Inc surged more than three percent on Tuesday after the bottler reported a smaller than expected first quarter loss, analysts said.
The company, which is 44 percent owned by Coca-Cola Co, reported a $0.24 per share loss, not counting a $0.03 charge for the redemption of long-term debt.
David Goldman of Robinson-Humphrey said the outcome compared favorably with expectations on Wall Street, where some analysts had expected Coke Enterprises to lose about $0.30 a share in the period.

Coke Enterprises stock was up 1-7/8 or 3.4 percent at 57-1/2 in afternoon trading on the New York Stockk Exchange. At the same time, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was 99.14 points or 1.54 percent higher.
Goldman attributed the Atlanta-based bottler's smaller-than-expected loss to smaller selling, general and administrative expenses and lower interest expenses.
